story.title: Kennedy Center Board Votes to Close Amid Legal Dispute Over Trump's Name
story.summary: The Kennedy Center board voted to temporarily close the performing arts center, citing financial issues and the need for renovations. This decision followed a federal judge's ruling that blocked the board from adding President Trump's name to the building or grounds. The closure comes amid tensions, as Trump threatened to cancel a significant renovation project if his name was not reinstated.

related_stories.title: Trump Critiques Supreme Court Justices Over Mail-In Voting Ruling
related_stories.summary: Trump expressed dissatisfaction with some Supreme Court Justices for their ruling on mail-in voting, which he believed did not align with his expectations. This ruling has provided clarity for voters and election officials ahead of the upcoming midterm elections, as it blocked the Trump administration from imposing new restrictions on mail ballots. The Supreme Court's decisions are seen as a setback for Trump's efforts to limit mail-in voting.

related_stories.title: EU Proposes Canada as First Associate Member Amid Strengthening Ties
related_stories.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has proposed that Canada become the European Union's first 'associate member,' a status not currently defined in EU treaties. This announcement was made during her annual State of the Union address, where she highlighted shared democratic values and common interests between the EU and Canada. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, present at the event, expressed interest in forming a unique alliance with the EU without seeking full membership.

related_stories.title: Trump Threatens to Keep Kennedy Center Closed Amid Name Change Dispute
related_stories.summary: Following a judge's ruling that President Trump's name cannot be reinstated on the Kennedy Center without congressional approval, Trump has threatened to halt renovations and keep the center closed indefinitely. The decision has sparked controversy regarding the future of the iconic arts institution.
